mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises real interest rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced corporate revenue expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply-side shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and profit pressure, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered periods, or the effect reverses during a wage inflation surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the relationship breaks down during a commodity price surge.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the 10-year Treasury yield (not directly observed but inferred from yield curve inversion proxies) signals a flattening yield curve, which historically precedes equity market declines over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while long-term yields fall (implied)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during episodes of implied yield curve flattening, or the pattern fails during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) where PAYEMS rises while RSAFS falls by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a savings-driven demand pullback, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises and RSAFS falls > -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 55% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during a fiscal stimulus period.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in average hourly earnings (not directly observed but inferred from labor market weakness) during a monetary tightening cycle amplifies recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4pp during FEDFUNDS tightening cycle
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a wage growth acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and S&P 500 returns exists during expansionary monetary policy regimes, such that a month-over-month increase in HOUST of more than 2% predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST rises > 2% but S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of expansionary regime months, or the relationship reverses during a housing supply shock.
